name: World Happiness Report
publisher: Gallup / Oxford Wellbeing Research Centre / UN SDSN
methodology_note:
Rankings use a three-year average of Gallup World Poll life-evaluation answers (Cantril ladder, 0-10); India's score: 2017 4.315, 2018 4.190, 2019 4.015, 2024 4.054, 2025 4.389, 2026 4.536 (per Wikipedia's tables of the reports). Number of countries varies each year. Gaps: out_of not confirmed for 2013, 2015, 2020, 2022 (omitted); the 2014 and 2012 editions are not included; a 2016 total of 156 (PTI/Scroll) vs 157 (other outlets) is reported. 2022 rank 136 is confirmed by a later report referring to it; 2020's 144 is also cited by a 2012-2026 review. 2017/2018/2019/2020/2022/2024 per-point links go to the edition's landing page, with the rank taken from Wikipedia's summary tables of those reports. No official Indian government rebuttal located.

Number of countries varies each year. Gaps: out_of not confirmed for 2013, 2015, 2020, 2022 (omitted); the 2014 and 2012 editions are not included; a 2016 total of 156 (PTI/Scroll) vs 157 (other outlets) is reported. 2022 rank 136 is confirmed by a later report referring to it; 2020's 144 is also cited by a 2012-2026 review. 2017/2018/2019/2020/2022/2024 per-point links go to the edition's landing page, with the rank taken from Wikipedia's summary tables of those reports. No official Indian government rebuttal located. The 2012 point (111th of 156, score 4.772) is from the first World Happiness Report, which was the only edition before 2013; there were no 2004-2011 editions. The 2012 report used 2005-2011 averages and a different country set/method from the 2013 edition, so the identical 2012 and 2013 ranks are not directly comparable.
